mei2024slang: Language evolves rapidly online through slang and memes, but LLMs trained on static corpora cannot adapt without costly continual retraining. SLANG is a benchmark that continuously integrates fresh data and tests how well models grasp emerging concepts. FOCUS, a companion method, uses causal inference to connect new phrases with real contextual instances of their colloquial use, rather than memorizing isolated definitions. Experiments on internet slang and memes show FOCUS improves precision and relevance over baselines, offering a way to adapt models to linguistic change without retraining.
mei2025not: Jailbreak evaluations often flag outputs as successful breaches when they are actually hallucinated and therefore harmless, inflating perceived risk. BABY BLUE is a benchmark and validation framework that adds specialized evaluators to check whether a jailbroken answer actually gives useful malicious instructions. It also augments existing red-teaming datasets with cases that isolate hallucinated jailbreaks. The result lets red-teamers measure the real harm potential of outputs rather than counting any off-policy reply as an attack, making safety evaluation more precise.
mei2026gated: Test-time adaptation for long contexts updates transient working-memory parameters, but uniform write policies waste gradient steps on low-value text and suffer high variance. GDWM reframes adaptation as budget-constrained memory consolidation: a Write Controller estimates Contextual Utility, an information-theoretic measure of how much each context region relies on long-range information, and allocates gradient steps accordingly under a coverage constraint. On ZeroSCROLLS and LongBench v2 it matches or beats uniform baselines with four times fewer gradient steps, advancing the efficiency-performance trade-off for test-time long-context adaptation.
mei2026hiddenguard: Refusal-based safety is binary: it either blocks a whole answer or grants it, causing over-censorship of benign requests and missing subtle harmful content. HiddenGuard adds PRISM, a representation router that runs alongside the model and uses intermediate hidden states for token-level, real-time detection and redaction of sensitive content. Instead of refusing, it selectively redacts or replaces harmful spans while keeping the rest of the answer informative. With a token-level annotated dataset across diverse contexts, it reaches over 90 percent F1 in detecting and redacting harmful spans, enabling nuanced context-aware moderation.
mei2026steep: Reasoning LLMs still hallucinate and fail to self-correct over long steps, and chain-of-thought offers no way to validate intermediate steps. Environment Augmented Generation gives each step real-time execution feedback, explores alternative branches when a step fails, and learns from successful trajectories, enabling deliberate backtracking and replanning. The resulting a1-32B model matches larger systems such as o1 on competition mathematics and beats similar models by up to 24.4 points. Analysis shows a steep scaling pattern: early investment in environment interaction pays off more as task complexity grows.
meng2024llm: A-star guarantees valid paths but grows expensive with state space, while LLMs reason globally over environments but make invalid or inefficient routes. LLM-A-star combines the two: the LLM supplies global environmental understanding to guide and prune the search, while A-star ensures path validity. The hybrid reduces the time and memory cost of exact planning in large-scale scenarios without sacrificing route correctness, showing that LLMs are best used to steer classical search rather than replace it.
rawlekar2026finding: Self-supervised DINO ViTs discover objects through  CLS attention, but that token summarizes the whole image and localizes objects poorly. Analyzing patch-level query, key, and value similarities across all layers, the work finds object-centric information encoded in all three components and distributed across the network rather than confined to the final layer. Object-DINO exploits this training-free: it clusters attention heads across layers by patch similarity and selects the object-centric cluster. It improves unsupervised object discovery by 3.6 to 12.4 CorLoc points and grounds objects to reduce multimodal LLM hallucination.
shen2025oida: The Opioid Industry Documents Archive contains millions of pages of legal and corporate records, requiring multimodal analysis of text, images, and layout. OIDA-QA organizes these documents into 400K training and 10K test items, extracts text, visual, and layout features, and uses multiple AI models to build 360K training and 10K test question-answering pairs. Domain-specific multimodal models grounded with historical QA pairs and page-level citations, plus an importance-based page classifier, improve answer precision. The released benchmark and open dataset support research on analyzing large corporate document archives.
shen2026fastcar: Auto-regressive video generation needs far more tokens than image generation, and decode-time MLPs dominate latency while adjacent frames produce highly redundant MLP outputs. FastCar replays cached MLP outputs from the previous frame when a Temporal Attention Score indicates the current frame is similar, backed by a theoretical analysis of when replay is safe. An FPGA accelerator with dynamic resource scheduling realizes the idea on edge hardware. It outperforms sparse-attention approaches with over 2.1 times decoding speedup and better energy efficiency, and combined with sparse attention it reduces drifting for long high-resolution videos.
song2026hard: Rendering text into compressed images lets multimodal models read ultra-long contexts, but degrading image resolution unexpectedly breaks safety alignment even when the text stays legible. Experiments across noise and geometric distortions show state-of-the-art defenses deteriorate sharply, attributed to cognitive overload: deciphering degraded inputs consumes attention that would otherwise audit safety. A simple structured cognitive offloading pipeline that separates visual transcription from safety assessment mitigates the bypass. The finding warns that vision-based context compression creates a security hole in multimodal alignment.
song2026mimolp: Subgraph-based link prediction is accurate because it uses local structure, but per-query subgraph message passing is slow. MIMO-LP multiplexes a batch of query pairs whose subgraphs come from one shared graph, superposing their message passing into a common latent space with minimal interference. Multiple queries are then processed in a single forward pass at training and inference, cutting redundant computation on overlapping subgraph regions. It runs up to 44 times faster than one-to-one subgraph methods while keeping predictive accuracy comparable.
sun2026pas: Video LLMs are temporally unstable: small frame-time shifts flip attention, because extending Rotary Position Embeddings to video creates an inverse-Fourier time kernel with frame-scale ripples that weight adjacent frames differently. PAS adds small opposed phase offsets across attention heads and averages their outputs, preserving per-head spectrum magnitude while smoothing the temporal kernel and attenuating high-frequency ripples. The training-free module makes attention Lipschitz-stable to small temporal shifts and improves several video-understanding benchmarks at matched token budgets with negligible cost, as a plug-and-play upgrade for temporal encoding.
